subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow early feedback only, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The requested optimization crosses Telegram ingress ordering, audio preflight, TTS delivery, caching, and session-state semantics, so code inspection cannot safely choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Stage the design around measured async STT/TTS
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad canonical tracker, handle #96278/#58887 as the narrow typing-cue slice if proven, then design async delivery with explicit ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks.

options.title: Limit scope to early feedback and delivery modes
options.body: Treat immediate typing cues and separate text/voice delivery as the supported near-term UX fixes while leaving deeper queueing/streaming/caching unplanned.

options.title: Close broad pipeline work as out of scope
options.body: Reject background voice pipeline changes for now and require users to tune existing audio/TTS timeouts and provider choices instead.

recommendation.title: Stage the design around measured async STT/TTS
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad canonical tracker, handle #96278/#58887 as the narrow typing-cue slice if proven, then design async delivery with explicit ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks.

likelyOwner.reason: The voice/TTS and queue-order history makes this the best available owner signal for deciding the pipeline contract.
